title: When the Letter Burns
premise: In the river town of Vellmora, on the eve of revolution, Freya Reyes has survived three years of occupation by keeping her head down in her father's print shop. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the ledger bearing every name of the resistance—including her father's—Freya must copy and smuggle the evidence past three checkpoints before the spring ice breaks and the river route closes forever. Guided by a half-remembered love for Tomas, a soldier now stationed at the second checkpoint, she learns that invisibility was always an illusion: memory itself is contraband. The book ends with Freya burning the original letter to draw the guards' eyes while the copies slip downstream, saving the town's names at the cost of the shop—and choosing, finally, to be seen.
about_author: Edmund Yarrow is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring printing equipment in Eastern European museum archives. His novels explore how ordinary craftspeople become unwilling witnesses to history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Letters
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Introduces the print shop, her father's typeface cutting, and the unspoken rules of survival under occupation. She sorts type by candlelight while soldiers patrol outside. Emotional beat: the comfort and suffocation of invisibility.

chapters.title: Requisition Orders
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Army officers announce the requisition of the town; a clerk demands all business ledgers, including the shop's, which secretly holds coded names. Her father burns one page too slowly. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Father's POV via found journal entries read by Freya. Reveals he encoded resistance names in kerning marks and margin notes. Emotional beat: Freya realizes her father trusted her with silence all along.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Disguised as a delivery girl carrying funeral announcements, she passes the mill checkpoint with copied pages sewn into her coat lining. A near-search leaves her shaking. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into competence.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A soldier at the second checkpoint watches the frozen river and remembers a girl from the print shop. He falsifies a cargo manifest to protect someone he cannot name. Emotional beat: duty beginning to crack like the ice.

chapters.title: The Widow's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She shelters with Marta, a widow who feeds resistance couriers and teaches Freya which silences are weapons rather than shields. Emotional beat: belonging found among strangers.

chapters.title: Names in the Margins
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Deciphering more of the ledger, she finds her own name among the protected—a list her father made years ago. Emotional beat: grief and pride entwined.

chapters.title: Orders to Search
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Commandant Brandt orders full body searches at checkpoint two after a courier escapes. Tomas volunteers for night shift hoping to control who searches whom. Emotional beat: complicity tightening around him.

chapters.title: A Face Across the Barrier
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At checkpoint two, Freya and Tomas recognize each other. He waves her through without searching her coat, both knowing what it costs. Emotional beat: love rekindled in the space between duty and betrayal.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Someone in the widow's network is reporting movements; a courier vanishes. Suspicion falls on everyone. Emotional beat: trust fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Questioned about the missing courier, Freya deploys three years of learned silences and walks out—but knows they will return for her father. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into cold clarity.

chapters.title: What My Father Cut
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Freya's POV. Memory of age twelve, learning to cut a letterform, her father saying every letter carries its shadow. Emotional beat: inheritance of craft as inheritance of courage.

chapters.title: The Second Copy
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The network prepares duplicate sets of pages so no single courier carries everything. Marta chooses Freya for the final run because she is 'the one nobody looks at.' Emotional beat: reluctant faith passed on.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The bridge checkpoint, commanded by Brandt himself, where papers are matched against faces. Freya turns back, plan broken, as the ice begins to groan downstream. Emotional beat: despair at the narrowing window.

chapters.title: Manifests and Mercy
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas discovers Brandt plans to burn the ledger and execute the named men before the thaw. He must decide whether to warn the girl or protect his company. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tomas slips a note into a returned proof sheet; Freya reads it by hiding it inside a hymnal during chapel. They meet once, briefly, in the granary. Emotional beat: two people choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: Burning the Original
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Plan formed: destroy the ledger's most damning pages publicly to fix the army's attention on the shop while copies go downriver with the ice break. Her father insists on lighting the fire himself. Emotional beat: sacrifice embraced, not endured.

chapters.title: The Night of Ash
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The shop burns; Brandt rages at the lost evidence; Tomas lets the 'arsonist' escape his patrol; Marta's traitor is exposed and quietly dealt with. Emotional beat: chaos as cover, grief as fuel.

chapters.title: When the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At dawn the river cracks open. Freya rides the first barge through checkpoint three with the final pages hidden in a coffin of printed mourning broadsheets. Tomas stands guard and does not look away. Emotional beat: passage through death toward life.

chapters.title: Delivered
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The pages reach the exile committee across the border; names are published in a free press pamphlet set in type cut from her father's patterns. Emotional beat: vindication that feels like mourning.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Names
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Court-martialed but spared when witnesses speak, Tomas deserts and follows the river north. Emotional beat: a man learning to belong to his choices rather than his uniform.

chapters.title: Setting New Type
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. In a rebuilt shop upstream, Freya cuts a new typeface and prints the town's restored roll of names. Tomas arrives at the door as the presses start. Emotional beat: love and memory made permanent in ink—the end of hiding.
